title: [23/03/2025] Different sources of air pollutants
prompt: The graph below shows different sources of air pollutants in the UK from 1990 to 2005. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the levels of air pollutants from three different sources in the UK over a 15-year period from 1990 to 2005.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, although transport was the only sector with increasing emissions, two other sources showed declining trends, resulting in lower total emissions. Additionally, industry remained the largest contributor to air pollution in the UK despite its significant reduction over time.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the major emission sources, industry generated approximately 5.8 million tonnes in 1990, nearly six times higher than both transport and household pollutants at around 1 million tonnes each. Thereafter, this sector experienced the most dramatic reduction, declining steadily to around 3 million tonnes by 1996 before falling further to roughly 2 million tonnes by 2005. Similarly, domestic emissions followed a downward trend on a smaller scale, dropping to approximately 0.5 million tonnes by 1996 and declining further to 0.2 million tonnes in the final year. In contrast, transport’s pollution output increased gradually from 1 million tonnes to around 1.4 million tonnes by 2005. Consequently, total air pollutants decreased significantly from approximately 7 million tonnes in 1990 to around 3.2 million tonnes by 2005, primarily driven by these substantial reductions in industrial and household sources.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: While individual sources showed mixed trends, total air pollutants demonstrated a consistent decline throughout the period. Starting at approximately 7 million tonnes in 1990, total emissions fell steadily to around 5 million tonnes by 1996 before continuing to decrease to roughly 3.2 million tonnes by 2005. This represents a substantial reduction of nearly 55% over the 15-year period.
